briefing.opening: Good day. We begin the Climate Briefing for November 14, 2026. Grounded in scientific facts, we deliver reportage on the severity of the climate crisis confronting the world and the domestic and international response efforts underway to overcome it.

sections.title: 🔴 COP31 Summit Faces Impasse Amid UN's Strong Warnings on Emissions Reductions
sections.content: At the ongoing COP31 summit in Antalya, Türkiye, the UN Secretary-General reiterated an urgent call for immediate and bold greenhouse gas emissions cuts to avert climate catastrophe [30, 55, 59, 65]. Delivering the stark message that "peace cannot be built on a burning planet," leaders of climate-vulnerable nations also pleaded for emergency action; however, the global response regarding climate finance support remains tepid [30, 53, 73]. Compounding the challenges, the absence of key leaders such as Mark Carney and the heavy presence of over 100 fossil fuel-affiliated companies and lobby groups have intensified venue friction and debates over climate science [64, 66, 75]. In response, the European Union (EU) affirmed its stance to defend climate science, while citizen power was reaffirmed as a decisive weapon against global warming [42, 60].

sections.title: ⚠️ Super El Niño and Climate Change Trigger Ecological and Public Health Crises
sections.content: The combination of Super El Niño and global warming is dealing a direct blow to marine ecosystems and the health of vulnerable populations worldwide. In Monterey Bay, California, an unprecedented die-off was recently documented, with large numbers of dead marine organisms, including birds and sea lions, discovered following rapid water temperature spikes and high tides [78]. Furthermore, climate shocks driven by El Niño have not only exacerbated Indonesia's wildfire crisis but also sparked warnings that millions of women in crisis-affected areas face heightened risks of maternal mortality [56, 76]. Compounding these concerns, studies report that severe anxiety over climate change is leading to diminished quality of life during pregnancy, underscoring how the climate crisis is expanding into an everyday public health issue [63].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 South Korea–Nepal Climate Agreement Signed Alongside Domestic Carbon Neutrality Drive
sections.content: South Korea has joined hands with Nepal to establish a foundation for cross-border climate action and the revitalization of international greenhouse gas reduction projects [1, 2]. The two countries officially signed a framework agreement on climate change cooperation, agreeing to accelerate joint efforts to bolster developing countries' emissions mitigation capacities and secure tangible reduction outcomes [4, 9, 69]. Local communities across Korea are also driving the transition forward: Jeju Province has launched an initiative to become the first "Climate Economy Capital" linked to residents' income, while the Incheon Urban Development Corporation signed an agreement for solar power projects to accelerate renewable energy expansion [13, 27]. Across schools and public institutions, grassroots carbon reduction activities are gaining traction, including zero-food-waste carbon-neutral meal operations and rail-centered climate action campaigns [12, 14].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Renewable Grid Interconnection and Outlook for Low-Carbon Industrial Transition
sections.content: Driven by the expansion of renewable energy and demand for power grid modernization, the electrical equipment and smart grid markets are projected to enter a long-term growth trajectory through 2035 [22, 23, 25]. Global investments in critical grid-interconnection infrastructure—including substations, high-voltage power transformers, and phase sequence indicators—are providing robust support for a stable clean energy transition [24, 25, 26]. Meanwhile, the development of the hydrogen economy is accelerating, with China's renewable-based hydrogen production capacity exceeding 350,000 tons per year; however, seamlessly linking production, transport, and demand remains a major challenge [28]. Public consensus for the energy transition and emissions regulation is also solidifying, with an international poll showing that 85% of citizens across 18 countries support measures to curb methane emissions [37].

briefing.closing: Even amid divisions within the international community, the scientific community's warnings urging emissions cuts and the broader momentum toward an energy transition are growing increasingly clear. This concludes today's Climate Briefing.
